messages: marisa: Quick sync — proposing we move console forms to progressive validation: validate on blur for fields, show a compact error summary at the top only when there are >1 errors, and keep inline errors minimal. For destructive actions, recommend tiered confirmations (undo toast for cheap deletes, typed confirm for org-level deletes). Thoughts? oliver: Like the progressive idea. My concern: required fields visibility. If we only validate on blur, users who tab past might miss requiredness until submit. Do we keep an asterisk? gina: Accessibility note: an asterisk alone is not sufficient. If you show an asterisk visually, make the label read as "Required" for screen readers (e.g., add visually-hidden text or aria-label). Also ensure error summary anchors move focus into the field and include aria-invalid=true on invalid inputs. samir: From an implementation POV progressive validation = fewer full-form re-renders which is good. We can reuse the existing ErrorSummary component but make a lightweight variant. Example anchor pattern: `Missing email` and the link handler focuses the input and sets `aria-invalid`. marisa: Exactly — keep inline errors single-line and only show the detailed messages in the summary when it's shown. Inline: short phrase like "Required" or "Invalid email". Summary: full copy + path to field. taylor: On destructive actions: I want a concrete tiering: - Low (single item file delete): modal with clear primary/destructive button + undo toast - Medium (project-level delete): typed confirm (enter name) + danger styling - High (org-level / irreversible): typed confirm + cooldown (5s) + admin-only scope This gives consistent affordances across Console. oliver: Agree. Copy examples: "Type the project name to permanently delete 'analytics'" or "Type DELETE to confirm permanent deletion" — prefer the name-based pattern for clarity. gina: For the typed confirm inputs: label must be explicit and accessible (e.g., ``). Ensure color contrast for placeholders and error text. Also announce the countdown for cooldowns to screen readers. samir: Implementation note: we'll need a small state machine for the typed confirm + cooldown + retry lockouts. I'll draft a tiny spec and copy a token from the existing modal system so we don't get style drift. marisa: Also: propose an optional compact summary toggle in user settings for power users — they can hide the top summary and rely on inline errors. Would reduce noise for frequent form users. oliver: Can we do a quick A/B? summary-visible vs summary-hidden, measure time-to-success and error rates. marisa: Yes — I'll set up a short prototype and run 10 quick tasks with PMs/SDRs. gina: I'll write a11y checklist for the specs (aria-required, aria-invalid, error summary roles, focus management). samir: I'll PR a lightweight ErrorSummary component (compact variant) and wire the focus anchors. marisa: Great. Action items: 1) marisa — prototype microcopy + flows, 2) samir — component PR w/ anchors, 3) gina — a11y checklist, 4) oliver/taylor — confirm tier definitions + copy. I'll ping next week with the prototype link. :thumbsup: designbot: Snapshot created for thread 1719876543 — prototype branch: feat/compact-validation oliver: :+1: Looking forward to the prototype. taylor: :thinking_face: One more ask — include keyboard-only flows in the prototype (no mouse). marisa: Good call. Will add keyboard-only test steps. samir: Noted — will ensure anchor focus works with keyboard nav. gina: Thanks — I can run a quick screen-reader pass once the prototype is ready. marisa: Thanks everyone!
